paragraphs: I am 宗宮大輝, and I was allowed to study abroad for about three months from March 2018 at the Medical University of Gdansk in Poland. Looking back, I feel once again that it was truly a fulfilling few months. Based on this study abroad, I would like to write about the clerkship at the Medical University of Gdansk and what I felt through studying abroad.

The official language of Poland is of course Polish, but at this Medical University of Gdansk there are two courses, the Polish Division and the English Division. The former is, as the name says, for Polish students, whereas the latter provides medical education in English for international students from various countries. The students of the English Division come from a very wide range of countries, such as Sweden, Saudi Arabia, the United Kingdom, the United States, India, Spain, Italy, Iraq and Sri Lanka. Compared with other study abroad destinations, I feel that being able to interact with students from so many countries is a great strength of the Medical University of Gdansk. In fact, I was able to have the very valuable experience of talking with students from Italy, Saudi Arabia, Sweden and Poland about their countries' medicine, religion and customs.

Together with the English Division students, I rotated for one to three weeks through diabetes and hypertension, cardiology, cardiac surgery, allergology, pulmonary medicine, pediatrics, and obstetrics and gynecology. The flow of a day was basically a lecture in the morning, then moving to the ward or outpatient clinic to do the clerkship. Because patients basically speak only Polish, it was difficult for us to take histories and do physical examinations on our own, but in every department the doctor in charge translated our questions and what the patient said. In addition, since I rotated through various departments, I had to learn a lot of medical English, but thanks to the lectures in each department I was able to learn English words little by little through them. Furthermore, in every department there was a written exam or oral examination on the last day of the clerkship, and I had to pass them, so preparing for them was very good study. In particular, the cardiology exam asked two questions drawn from more than 100 electrocardiograms in a textbook called "ECGs by Example," and thanks to this exam I think I became able to read ECGs considerably better than before.

One of the things that strongly impressed me during the clerkship was the large number of female doctors. In every department where I did clerkships, women made up about half, and I was surprised at the big difference from Japan. In Poland maternity leave and childcare leave are well provided, and I felt that this creates an environment in which women find it easy to work, and I thought that Japan too must learn from Poland.

Climate. When I arrived in early March, the minimum temperature was about -5℃, and since I had come from Nagoya, which was beginning to warm up, I felt it was very cold. But I was told that a week before I arrived it had been about -15℃, which shocked me. Gdansk is harsh in the cold during March, but in April it exceeds 10℃ and becomes a warm and comfortable climate. The scenery, brown and bleak when I had just arrived, gradually turned green through April and May and changed greatly, as if it were a completely different place.

Public safety and prices. Public safety is very good, and even when I was out walking late at night, I was never caught up in any trouble. And prices are very low even within Europe (one half to one third of Japan's), which was very welcome for me, who wanted to keep living costs down.

Interaction with local students. Because I did the clerkship mixed in with other exchange students, I could interact with many students. Also, the dormitory where I lived day to day housed exchange students and Polish students, so I had many opportunities to interact with them. My best memory is the international party where everyone cooks and brings the food of their own country. It is a good memory that I made ramen that I had brought from Japan and everyone happily ate it. Besides this, various drinking parties are held, so you quickly make many friends.

Wanting to do things during this study abroad that I could only do now, I attended a dance class introduced to me by Professor Wozniak every Monday and Wednesday and learned Polish traditional dance. Most of the members of the dance class could speak only Polish, but they tried to teach me somehow with gestures, and I was very happy that they were kind to a student who had suddenly come from Japan. Thanks to their careful guidance and practice, I became able to dance a little of a traditional dance called Krakowiak, which was a very good once-in-a-lifetime experience.
There were also singing lessons at the same place, and I was able to learn the Polish national anthem too.

These three months were without a doubt the most fulfilling time of my life so far. Every day was stimulating in everything, the clerkship, daily life and extracurricular activities. And what I felt most strongly through this study abroad was the high level of the local students. In this university's English Division, students apparently have to pass several difficult tests before reaching the fourth year, when the clinical clerkship begins, and probably because of that, I felt that even fourth-year students are very knowledgeable. They were also all very ambitious, and I felt strongly that excellent students gather from countries all over the world, and as a Japanese I was able to think that I must work hard so as not to lose to them, which was a very good stimulus. What I learned in these three months will become irreplaceable in my life from now on.

I am truly grateful to the doctors of the International Collaboration Office, the alumni doctors of the Frontier Society, everyone in the Academic Affairs office, the doctors of Gdansk University, 島村君, who got through the three months of study abroad together with me, and the various other people who gave me enormous support, who supported me greatly for a long time from the preparation period before study abroad until after my return. Thank you very much.
